title: What Is a Tech Recruiter? (September 2026)
summary: A breakdown of tech recruiter duties, salary ranges, and fractional recruiting costs for startups, updated October 2026.
body_markdown:
You’ve likely wondered what exactly[tech recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) do and whether they’re worth working with when you’re trying to build your engineering team. The challenge comes down to understanding their role and figuring out whether a tech recruiter or fractional recruiter can help you find the right technical talent, without breaking your budget or wasting your time. So let’s break down where tech recruiters can help you, the cost of hiring one, and what your decision should be based on as a startup founder.


**TLDR:**


-


Tech recruiters specialize in technical roles. Compensation varies by seniority, location, and whether pay includes commission, bonuses, or equity; the cited salary table below separates base pay from total compensation.


-


Strong recruiters combine technical fluency with cultural assessment skills, which can help find suitable candidates faster when screening criteria are clear.


-


Fractional recruiters can offer a lower-cost alternative to salary-based agency placement fees, depending on search scope and hours required.


-


Some fractional recruiting marketplaces connect startups with vetted recruiters who work hourly without long-term contracts.


-


Some integrated recruiting tools pair a free ATS with on-demand recruiter access so hiring teams and recruiters share one pipeline from day one.


## What Are Tech Recruiters


Tech recruiters are talent acquisition professionals who focus on filling technical roles, such as software engineers, data scientists, DevOps engineers, cybersecurity specialists, and technical leadership positions. Unlike general recruiters, they build deep knowledge of programming languages and the skill sets engineering roles require.


For startups, working with recruiters who understand early-stage hiring can be the difference between landing top talent and losing candidates to larger companies with more developed recruiting processes.


## Key Responsibilities of Tech Recruiters


Tech recruiters handle work that goes beyond posting jobs and scheduling interviews. Their process starts with understanding each role’s technical requirements, often working with engineering teams to define required skills and the ideal candidate profile.


Key responsibilities include:


-


Writing role-specific job descriptions that reflect the technical stack and engineering expectations, instead of generic listings that could apply to any software role


-


Sourcing through technical channels like Wellfound, Dice, LinkedIn, and GitHub, finding candidates with relevant contributions instead of waiting on inbound applications


-


Conducting technical phone screens that assess depth of experience in specific languages, frameworks, or systems before candidates reach engineering teams


-


Coordinating technical interview loops, including take-home assignments, system design rounds, and panel interviews with the right engineering stakeholders


-


Managing offer negotiations, including base salary, equity, signing bonuses, and remote or hybrid arrangements that technical candidates often weigh carefully


Tech recruiters also serve as market intelligence resources, tracking salary trends and hiring activity. This work can improve the speed and quality of technical hires when screening criteria are clear.


## How Tech Recruiters Work


The workflow of successful tech recruiters combines systematic processes with relationship-driven approaches. Most begin each search with a detailed intake session with the hiring team, spending time on team dynamics, technical architecture, and growth plans.


Their sourcing strategies include mining GitHub for developers with relevant contributions, participating in technical communities like Reddit’s programming subreddits, and maintaining relationships with candidates from previous searches.


Screening typically involves multiple touchpoints: an initial phone screen on technical background and career motivations, then a deeper technical conversation or a brief coding exercise. The evaluation phase requires recruiters to weigh technical assessments, cultural fit, and practical considerations like salary expectations and timeline before presenting candidates with detailed profiles covering resume, motivation, strengths, and potential concerns.


Modern tech recruiters also use applicant tracking systems, sourcing tools, and increasingly AI-assisted tools to manage large candidate volumes.


## Tech Recruiter Salary Information


Tech recruiter pay varies by experience, location, and company type. The ranges below match[KORE1’s 2026 salary guide](https://www.kore1.com/tech-recruiter-salary-guide/) . KORE1 is a staffing firm, so its figures work best as one market reference.


Level Experience Base Salary (Annual) Total Compensation (with Bonus, Commission, or Equity)


Sourcer or Recruiting Coordinator 0-2 years $50,000 to $68,000 $55,000 to $80,000


Technical Recruiter 2-4 years $70,000 to $95,000 $80,000 to $125,000


Senior Technical Recruiter 5-8 years $95,000 to $135,000 $115,000 to $190,000


Location also affects these ranges, as shown in[Indeed’s California technical recruiter salary data](https://www.indeed.com/career/technical-recruiter/salaries/CA) , and[KORE1’s salary guide](https://www.kore1.com/tech-recruiter-salary-guide/) distinguishes in-house base pay and equity from agency compensation that includes commission. Client fees are separate: fractional recruiters in Dover’s marketplace set their own hourly, retainer, or pay-per-hire rates, with total cost depending on scope.


## Finding the Right Tech Recruiter


Picking the right tech recruiter means weighing their technical knowledge against their track record with hiring challenges like yours.


-


Technical fluency: A quality tech recruiter should explain the difference between front-end and back-end work and why certain languages suit certain projects.


-


Track record: Ask for examples of challenging searches they’ve completed, particularly those involving similar company stages or technical requirements.


-


Communication: Recruiters who respond slowly or skip regular updates may struggle to compete for talent when candidates hold other offers.


-


Cultural assessment: Look for recruiters who ask thoughtful questions about company culture, team working styles, and growth stage challenges.


-


Transparency: Be wary of recruiters who make unrealistic promises about timeline, fees, or candidate quality, or who stay vague about sourcing strategies.


For startups, look for recruiters who grasp early-stage trade-offs: pitching equity and growth opportunities when salary alone can’t compete.


## Working with Tech Recruiters


Good partnerships with tech recruiters need clear communication and realistic expectations. Both sides should understand their roles and stay in regular contact during the search.


-


**Set clear expectations:** Define the ideal candidate profile, including must-have skills, nice-to-have skills, experience level, and cultural fit.


-


**Provide context:** Share team structure, technical challenges, growth plans, and culture so recruiters can represent the role accurately and assess fit.


-


**Maintain communication:** When recruiters present candidates, give timely feedback that goes beyond a simple yes or no.


-


**Define processes:** Strong candidates often have multiple offers, so a fast, well-organized interview process can be a competitive advantage. Set this up before the search starts.


-


**Set clear performance metrics:** Agree on how you’ll measure progress and how often you’ll review the search, so both sides share a baseline.


Watch for recruiters who submit unqualified candidates, skip candidate context, or push quick decisions. Quality recruiters focus on fit over volume and can offer useful insight on expectations and interview practices.


## The 2026 Tech Recruiting Environment


AI-assisted applications make verification an important part of technical recruiting. Startups do well to pair resume review with work samples, technical conversations, and reference checks, with people responsible for the final call.


Skills-based hiring is another useful consideration.[NACE’s Job Outlook 2026 survey findings](https://www.naceweb.org/job-market/trends-and-predictions/employer-use-of-skills-based-hiring-practices-grows) report growing use of skills-based hiring. The survey concerns college recruiting, so it’s not a census of technical hiring or proof degree requirements are gone. A recruiter who can discuss project experience and coordinate job-relevant assessments may matter more than one who matches resumes to credentials.


### AI Hiring Rules Add a Practical Check in 2026


AI-assisted screening also carries legal considerations. Illinois’[AI hiring law](https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/publicacts/view/103-0804) , effective January 1, 2026, bars covered businesses from using AI in ways that result in discrimination based on protected classes, and bars using ZIP codes as a proxy for them. Oversight of screening tools is now a practical part of a tech recruiter’s work.


As of October 2026, a useful question for a recruiting partner is how they review AI-assisted recommendations before candidates advance or get rejected. Clear criteria and human review help, but don’t prove compliance alone. Startups hiring across states may need legal guidance on which rules apply.


## Why Dover Fits Tech Recruiting for Startups


Startups may need hands-on recruiting support without adding a full-time recruiter.[Dover’s recruiter marketplace](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) connects them with vetted fractional recruiters who have startup hiring experience. Hourly work is the primary model, with retainer and pay-per-hire arrangements also available. Each recruiter sets their own rates, and clients agree on scope and budget with them. Dover reports an average cost per hire of $4,800 across all roles, not a guaranteed price for a technical search, with no long-term contracts required.


Hiring teams and fractional recruiters can work together in Dover’s free ATS, which lists unlimited users, jobs, and candidates on the free tier, as shown in Dover’s[current ATS plan comparison](https://www.dover.com/pricing) . Premium costs $199 per month and adds AI resume review and an AI interview notetaker. Recruiter services are paid separately from ATS access.


Dover’s recruiters bring startup hiring experience, and the model can support faster hiring and lower costs than traditional agencies, depending on role complexity and pricing model.


## FAQs


### When should I consider hiring a tech recruiter instead of recruiting myself?


Consider hiring a tech recruiter if recruiting is taking a large share of your week, you’re struggling to source qualified technical candidates, or you’re competing against larger companies for the same talent pool. Recruiters can be especially useful when you need to move quickly in competitive markets.


### Can fractional tech recruiters work with our existing hiring tools?


Yes, depending on the recruiter and the tools you use. The arrangement should define where candidate records live, who updates them, and what access the recruiter needs. Using one shared system can improve visibility, but it does not guarantee that records will always be complete or current.


### What hiring tools do most early-stage and YC startups use?


A lightweight stack for an early-stage startup can include an ATS to manage pipeline, a sourcing tool for outbound outreach, and a scheduling tool to reduce coordination overhead. Cost sensitivity and setup time matter for founders without dedicated recruiting ops support. Shared pipeline tracking can help hiring teams and fractional recruiters keep track of candidates as headcount grows, provided someone owns recordkeeping and follow-ups.


### What should a team check before choosing a free applicant tracking system?


For teams making their first few hires, a useful free ATS supports candidate tracking and team collaboration with manageable setup work. Free plans vary in history limits, scheduling, reporting, and AI features, so checking individual features matters. Software can organize the search, while a recruiter contributes sourcing and hiring judgment. Neither a free plan nor added recruiter support guarantees faster hires; the fit depends on your roles, team capacity, and process.


## Final Thoughts on Working with Tech Recruiters


As of October 2026, the right recruiting model depends on role complexity, hiring volume, and team bandwidth.[Tech recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) , agency, in-house, or fractional, add more value when they understand a team’s technical needs. Dover is one example: a free ATS paired with fractional recruiters offering hourly, retainer, and pay-per-hire options, described on its recruiter marketplace page. The useful comparison stays scope, cost structure, and fit for the work ahead.
